problem: Foreign keys are declared but SQLite does not enforce them unless PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON is set per connection. cites.db currently holds 15,708 of 66,059 rows whose cited_id is not in paper (about 24%), on 1,493 distinct ids.
fix: Run PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON on every connection (importer included), delete the dangling rows (or move them to a separate unresolved_refs table), and add a PRAGMA foreign_key_check to the import/CI checks.

problem: The importer never enables foreign keys, so only duplicate/self-cite violations raise IntegrityError. The comment 'cited paper not in the corpus (foreign key)' is wrong: out-of-corpus references are loaded, not skipped. The printed 'resolved 66059 of 66160 (99.8%)' is false; only 50,365 of 66,160 rows (76.1%) point at a corpus paper, and the 101 skipped are all duplicates.
fix: Execute PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON after connect, or check cited_id against paper explicitly. Count duplicates, out-of-corpus and self-cites separately in the report.

problem: Each row is inserted in its own transaction (with con:) and a bare except IntegrityError lumps every failure reason together. 66k commits is slow, and the con is never closed. A malformed row (non-integer, missing column) raises ValueError and aborts the run mid-way with a partial load.
fix: Use one transaction, INSERT OR IGNORE with explicit pre-checks to classify skips, validate rows, and close the connection.

problem: Syllabus ranking is distorted by the dangling edges. Because edges.tsv includes cited ids that are not in paper, those nodes absorb PageRank: ~20% of total rank sits on non-corpus ids, and all 25 of the top 25 printed results are non-corpus ids shown as '?'. This is why the syllabus looked odd; it is the data, not the papers.
fix: Fix the data first, then restrict the graph to corpus nodes in rank.py (filter edges to ids in paper) and fail or warn if titles.get(pid) is None.

problem: Exports every row of cites without checking that both ends exist in paper, so the dangling edges flow straight into ranking. It also writes edges.tsv to the cwd and silently overwrites it.
fix: Select with JOINs on paper for both citing_id and cited_id (or run foreign_key_check and abort), and have it take the output path as an argument.

problem: Joins paper, so it silently hides the out-of-corpus ids that the ranking shows, making the two views disagree. GROUP BY p.id with a non-aggregated p.title relies on SQLite leniency, and ties in citations have no deterministic ORDER BY.
fix: Add a tie-breaker (ORDER BY citations DESC, p.id) and GROUP BY p.id, p.title.

problem: LEFT JOIN paper returns NULL title/year for dangling cited_ids (which exist today), and ORDER BY p.year places those NULLs first.
fix: Remove dangling rows from the data, then use an inner JOIN, or order by p.year NULLS LAST, c.cited_id.

problem: ORDER BY p.year DESC has no tie-breaker, so the page order is unstable for papers from the same year.
fix: Add , p.id as a secondary sort key.

problem: README states that out-of-corpus references are rejected because cites.cited_id references paper(id). That is false without PRAGMA foreign_keys=ON and it is what hid the problem.
fix: Correct the README after enforcing the constraint, and document the real coverage figure.

problem: Index on cites(cited_id, citing_id) duplicates what is needed for the reverse lookup only partially: it is fine for cited_by.sql but, since cites is WITHOUT ROWID with PK (citing_id, cited_id), it is a full second copy of the table.
fix: Keep it (it serves cited_by.sql and most_cited.sql), but note the cost; no change required.
